paragraphs: PSTrax sells digital inventory and asset management software built for first responders. The system tracks inspections of vehicles, stations, equipment, supplies, controlled substances and blood products.

Rather than handing over a toolkit, the company builds and implements each system for the department and to that department's specs. Systems are meant to be ready to roll out in a matter of weeks. Ongoing support for changes is unlimited and comes at no extra cost. A one-year money back guarantee is offered to customers.

PSTrax, short for Public Safety Tracking Systems, was founded by Scott Bergeron and Cliff Long in 2009. It is headquartered in Littleton, Colorado, with 22 full-time employees. The company says it serves more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. That count includes more than 850 Fire-EMS agencies across the United States, Canada and Australia. It is privately held and says it answers to customers rather than to VC firms or shareholders. It reports a 98.5% customer retention rate.

quote.text: Creating a world where every first responder knows with certainty that their equipment, assets, and inventories are ready for the next call.
